parameters.name: per_page

parameters.name: scroll_param
parameters.description: The `scroll_param` from the previous response. Omit it to start a new scroll.

get.description:
The `list all companies` functionality does not work well for huge datasets, and can result in errors and performance problems when paging deeply. The Scroll API provides an efficient mechanism for iterating over all companies in a dataset.

- Each app can only have 1 scroll open at a time. Starting a second one returns a `400` error with code `scroll_exists`.
- If the scroll isn't used for 1 minute, it expires and calls with that scroll param return a `404` error with code `not_found`.
- If the end of the scroll is reached, `data` will be empty and the scroll parameter will expire.

The response always has `pages` and `total_count` set to `null`. Use `scroll_param` to fetch the next page.

{% admonition type="info" name="Scroll Parameter" %}
  You can get the first page of companies by simply sending a GET request to the scroll endpoint.
  For subsequent requests you will need to use the scroll parameter from the response.
{% /admonition %}
{% admonition type="danger" name="Scroll network timeouts" %}
  Since scroll is often used on large datasets network errors such as timeouts can be encountered. When this occurs you will see a HTTP 500 error with the following message:
  "Request failed due to an internal network error. Please restart the scroll operation."
  If this happens, you will need to restart your scroll query: It is not possible to continue from a specific point when using scroll.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `read_users_companies` OAuth scope.

sla_applied.title: Applied SLA
sla_applied.description:
The SLA Applied object contains the details for which SLA has been applied to this conversation.
Important: if there are any canceled sla_events for the conversation - meaning an SLA has been manually removed from a conversation, the sla_status will always be returned as null.

sla_name.description: The name of the SLA as given by the teammate when it was created.

sla_status.description:
SLA statuses:
            - `hit`: If there’s at least one hit event in the underlying sla_events table, and no “missed” or “canceled” events for the conversation.
            - `missed`: If there are any missed sla_events for the conversation and no canceled events. If there’s even a single missed sla event, the status will always be missed. A missed status is not applied when the SLA expires, only the next time a teammate replies.
            - `active`: An SLA has been applied to a conversation, but has not yet been fulfilled. SLA status is active only if there are no “hit, “missed”, or “canceled” events.

url.description: The relative URL of the note.

body.description: The body text of the note.

addressable_list.title: Addressable List
addressable_list.description: A list used to access other resources from a parent model.

id.description: The id of the addressable object

url.description: Url to get more company resources for this contact

company_data.title: Company Data
company_data.description: An object containing data about the companies that a contact is associated with.

id.description: The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom.

type.description: The type of the object. Always company.

url.description: The relative URL of the company.

social_profile.title: Social Profile
social_profile.description: A Social Profile allows you to label your contacts, companies, and conversations and list them using that Social Profile.

name.description: The name of the Social media profile

url.description: The name of the Social media profile

tag.title: Tag
tag.description: A tag allows you to label your contacts, companies, conversations, tickets, articles, internal articles, content snippets and external pages, and list them using that tag.

id.description: The id of the tag

applied_at.description: The time when the tag was applied to the object. Only present when the tag is returned as part of a tagging operation on a contact, conversation, ticket, article, internal article, content snippet, or external page, when listing the tags on a contact, or when it is returned as part of an external page. `null` when the tag has just been removed from an article, internal article, content snippet or external page. Removing a tag from a contact, conversation or ticket returns the original value.

applied_by.description: The admin who applied the tag. Only present when the tag is returned as part of a tagging operation on a contact, conversation, ticket, article, internal article, content snippet, or external page, when listing the tags on a contact, or when it is returned as part of an external page. `null` when the tag has just been removed from an article, internal article, content snippet or external page. Removing a tag from a contact, conversation or ticket returns the original value. When no admin is recorded, `type` is `nobody_admin` and `id` is `null`.

id.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom.

external_id.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is provided by the Client.

conversation_source_author.title: Conversation source author
conversation_source_author.description: The author who started the conversation. Can be a Contact, Admin, or Bot.

id.description: The id of the author.

part_attachment.title: Part attachment
part_attachment.description: The file attached to a part

content_type.description: The content type of the attachment

source_email_message_metadata.title: Email Message Metadata
source_email_message_metadata.description: Contains metadata if the message was sent as an email

message_id.description: The unique identifier for the email message as specified in the Message-ID header

email_address_headers.title: Email Address Headers
email_address_headers.description: A list of an email address headers.

history.description: The HTML content of any quoted or forwarded email history from the initial inbound message

ai_topic_subtopic.title: AI Topic and Subtopic
ai_topic_subtopic.description: A single AI-generated topic and subtopic classification for a conversation. Surfaced inside `custom_attributes` under the "AI Topic and Subtopic" key as an array of these objects. Requires the AI add-on; the key is omitted when the conversation has no classification.

topic_name.description: The name of the AI-generated topic.

subtopic_name.description: The name of the AI-generated subtopic, if any.

id.description: The id of the subtopic.

cx_score_reason.title: CX Score reason
cx_score_reason.description: A single reason behind a conversation's CX Score. Surfaced inside `custom_attributes` under the "CX Score reasons" key as an array of these objects.

value.description: The value recorded for the reason.

oneOf.title: string
oneOf.description: A date and time following the ISO8601 notation.

oneOf.title: integer
oneOf.description: A date and time as UNIX timestamp notation.

custom_object_instance_list.title: Custom Object Instances
custom_object_instance_list.description: The list of associated custom object instances for a given reference attribute on the parent object.

instances.description: The list of associated custom object instances for a given reference attribute on the parent object.

conversation_response_time.title: Conversation response time
conversation_response_time.description: Details of first response time of assigned team in seconds.

team_name.description: Name of the assigned Team, null if team does not exist, Unassigned if no team is assigned.

response_time.description: First response time of assigned team in seconds.

id.description: The ID of the linked object

category.description: Category of the Linked Ticket Object.

total_count.description: The total number of content sources used by AI Agent in the conversation.

content_sources.description: The content sources used by AI Agent in the conversation.

conversation_scorecard_reviewed_teammate.title: Reviewed Teammate
conversation_scorecard_reviewed_teammate.description: The teammate (or AI agent) whose handling of the conversation was reviewed by this scorecard.

type.description: The kind of reviewee. `ai` if the conversation was handled by Fin or scored without a specific teammate; `admin` if a specific teammate was reviewed.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who was reviewed. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_reviewer.title: Reviewer
conversation_scorecard_reviewer.description: Who the review of this scorecard is assigned to. `ai` when it is assigned to Fin; `admin` when it is assigned to a teammate. Null when no review exists for this scorecard or the review is unassigned.

type.description: The kind of reviewer. `ai` if the review is assigned to Fin; `admin` if it is assigned to a teammate.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin the review is assigned to. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_submitted_by.title: Submitted By
conversation_scorecard_submitted_by.description: Who last submitted the review of this scorecard, which can differ from the `reviewer` it is assigned to. `ai` when Fin submitted it; `admin` when a teammate did. Null while the review is unreviewed or when no review exists for this scorecard.

type.description: The kind of submitter. `ai` if Fin submitted the review; `admin` if a teammate did.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who submitted the review. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_revised_by.title: Revised By
conversation_scorecard_revised_by.description: Who last changed the review of this scorecard after it was submitted. `ai` when Fin made the change; `admin` when a teammate did. Null while the review is unreviewed, when it has not been changed since it was submitted, or when no review exists for this scorecard.

type.description: The kind of reviser. `ai` if Fin changed the review; `admin` if a teammate did.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who last changed the review. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_note.title: Scorecard Note
conversation_scorecard_note.description: A note a teammate left on the QA review of this scorecard.

id.description: The id of the note.

created_at.description: The time the note was created.

updated_at.description: The time the note was last edited. Equal to `created_at` when the note has never been edited.

body.description: The text of the note exactly as the teammate entered it. Plain text; it is not rendered as HTML.
body.example: Great empathy in the second reply.

conversation_scorecard_evaluator.title: Conversation Scorecard Evaluator
conversation_scorecard_evaluator.description: A single evaluator within a scorecard, including its result for this conversation.

evaluator_id.description: The unique identifier of the evaluator (criterion) within the scorecard.

name.description: The name of the evaluator (criterion). Null if the evaluator's name could not be resolved.

result.description: The evaluator's result for this conversation. Null if the evaluator was not scored.

email_address_header.title: Email Address Header
email_address_header.description: Contains data for an email address header for a conversation part that was sent as an email.

type.description: The type of email address header

name.description: The name associated with the email address

custom_object_instance.title: Custom Object Instance
custom_object_instance.description: A Custom Object Instance represents an instance of a custom object type. This allows you to create and set custom attributes to store data about your customers that is not already captured by Intercom. The parent object includes recommended default attributes and you can add your own custom attributes.

id.description: The Intercom defined id representing the custom object instance.

external_id.description: The id you have defined for the custom object instance.

external_created_at.description: The time when the Custom Object instance was created in the external system it originated from.

external_updated_at.description: The time when the Custom Object instance was last updated in the external system it originated from.

created_at.description: The time the attribute was created as a UTC Unix timestamp

updated_at.description: The time the attribute was last updated as a UTC Unix timestamp

type.description: The identifier of the custom object type that defines the structure of the custom object instance.

custom_attributes.description:
The custom attributes you have set on the custom object instance.

Each value is returned with the type of the attribute it is set on: a string, integer, number or boolean, or `null` when the attribute is unset. A list attribute returns the label of the selected option. A reference attribute returns an object holding the referenced records, under `contacts` for a contact reference, `conversations` for a conversation reference, or `instances` for a reference to another custom object type.

content_source.title: Content Source
content_source.description: The content source used by AI Agent in the conversation.

content_type.description: The type of the content source.

url.description: The internal URL linking to the content source for teammates.

title.description: The title of the content source.

locale.description: The ISO 639 language code of the content source.

conversation_scorecard_note_author.title: Note Author
conversation_scorecard_note_author.description: Who wrote the note. Null when the teammate who wrote it has since been deleted.

type.description: The kind of author. `admin` when a teammate wrote the note; `ai` when Fin did.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who wrote the note. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_evaluator_result.title: Conversation Scorecard Evaluator Result
conversation_scorecard_evaluator_result.description: The outcome of a single evaluator within a scorecard.

value.description: The evaluator's selected value (typically a label such as `pass`, `fail`, or a category identifier).

value_label.description: The label of the rating option matching `value` (for example `Needs improvement`). Omitted when the label could not be resolved.

source.description: The origin of the result (for example, `ai` or `human`).

reasoning.description: A free-text explanation of the result.
reasoning.example: The agent acknowledged the issue and resolved it within the same response.

reason_ids.description: Identifiers for structured reasons assigned to the result, if any.

reasons.description: The structured reasons chosen for this result. Omitted when none were chosen.

other_text.description: Free-text entered by the reviewer to supplement or stand in for the structured `reason_ids` — typically captured when the reviewer selects an "Other" option or adds a custom note. Null when not provided.
other_text.example: Agent acknowledged the issue but missed the follow-up question about billing.

conversation_scorecard_evaluator_reason.title: Evaluator Reason
conversation_scorecard_evaluator_reason.description: A single structured reason assigned to an evaluator's result.

name.description: The name of the reason. Null if the reason's name could not be resolved.
